original_2016_argument.claim: Because the site was exposed or very shallow around the Last Glacial Maximum, the preserved shape was interpreted as pointing to a very recent (Holocene) origin.

facts: >7000 pockmarks investigated in the Troll region
dating places formation in the initial Holocene
gas hydrate dissociation was modeled as likely trigger
comparative_preservation_controls.source: A climatic trigger for the giant Troll pockmark field in the northern North Sea, Earth and Planetary Science Letters 464 (2017)
comparative_preservation_controls.effect_on_sr004: Demonstrates that recognizable pockmark morphology can persist long after the formative fluid-release episode. Good preservation is not specific to a young impact.

facts: pockmarks show no evidence of recent gas/water expulsion
they nevertheless experienced reduced sedimentation rates through the Holocene
comparative_preservation_controls.source: Sediment mapping and long-term monitoring of currents and sediment fluxes in pockmarks in the Oslofjord, Norway, Marine Geology 346 (2013)
comparative_preservation_controls.effect_on_sr004: Shows a mechanism by which pockmark depressions can resist simple infill and remain morphologically expressed for long periods.

facts: one deep pockmark was interpreted to have formed before 10.1 ka BP
evidence suggests repeated activity through the Holocene
sub-seabed gas and pull-down/acoustic effects occur around pockmarks
comparative_preservation_controls.source: Spatial Relationships between Pockmarks and Sub-Seabed Gas in Fjordic Settings: Evidence from Loch Linnhe, West Scotland, Geosciences 11(7), 2021

facts: buried pockmarks span Holocene to Pleistocene stratigraphy
residual seabed topography can persist after burial/drape
pockmark conduits can be reused for later fluid migration
comparative_preservation_controls.source: Evidence for fluid migration following pockmark formation: Examples from the Nile Deep Sea Fan, Marine Geology 303-306 (2012)
Elongate depressions on the southern slope of the Norwegian Trench (Skagerrak): morphology and evolution, Marine Geology 146 (1998)

assessment.reason: Relict and long-lived pockmarks can preserve strong morphology for thousands of years, can experience reduced infill, and can be maintained or reactivated by currents or renewed fluid migration. Therefore morphology preservation cannot date SR-004 or discriminate impact from pockmark without stratigraphic dating.

required_age_tests: radiocarbon/OSL/other suitable dates through the complete 12.5 m central-core stratigraphy
identify basal crater-fill or erosional surface and directly date material above/below it
tie fill stratigraphy to regional sea-level and sedimentation history
if fluid escape is suspected, date methane-derived authigenic carbonate or seep-related fauna/mineral phases where possible
